newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says rebels barred from proposed conference.
newsitem.headline: France says rebels barred from proposed conference.

text.p: France said on Wednesday that Tutsi-led rebels threatening to topple Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko would be excluded from an international conference which Paris wants organised on the Zaire crisis.

"This is a conference to be attended by states and which is to be organised by the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity ," foreign ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux told reporters who asked him if the rebels would be invited.
France, which has long supported Mobutu, is urgently seeking such a conference to halt hostilities and prevent the break-up of Zaire.
Doutriaux was replying to questions about a statement in Paris on Tuesday by Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, who said he did not believe a conference would bring a quick solution to the crisis.

"I support the idea of an international conference but it is a medium or long-term arrangement. It cannot solve specific problems in the short run and you must have something more specific to deal with the Zaire situation," Museveni told a news conference after talks with French President Jacques Chirac.
"We believe the calling of a conference on security, peace and development for the region is a must," Doutriaux said.
The French official said that preparing such a conference was part of a brief given by the U.N. and the OAU to Algerian Mohammed Shanoun who has been delegated to visit the area.

Museveni had said he believed a more immediate solution to bring peace to Zaire would be to empower Sahnoun, backed by "some political heavyweight," to mediate a cease-fire between Zaire and the rebels.

The rebels have captured a swathe of Zairean territory along the borders with Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda and Paris suspects Kampala, with U.S. acquiescence, of aiding and abetting the Rwandan-backed rebels.
Paris believes the key to halting the conflict may lie with Washington which has close ties with Uganda and Rwanda.

After months of transatlantic squabbling over Africa, French officials say the Americans appear to have come round to their view that a collapse of Zaire could destabilise the whole of Central Africa and would not be in U.S. interests.

The United States backs the proposed conference. But sceptics say Washington may be paying lip service to the idea to placate Paris while hoping the rebellion will have spread to Kinshasa before the conference gets off the ground.
